record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: For a three-dimensional Robertson-Walker brane coupled to a scalar field in a five-dimensional bulk, do regular asymptotic solutions exist, and if so can they support the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant while accounting for the role of curvature and the comparison with the Minkowski-brane case?

evidence.quote:
4.1 RW branes and scalar ﬁelds
The singularity structure and the corresponding asymptotic behavior of a 3D RW brane coupled to a scalar ﬁeld in a ﬁve-dimensional bulk can be analyzed in full generality using the method of asymptotic splittings. One central issue is to examine the existence of regular solutions, and in accordance with the self-tuning proposal, to address the cosmological constant problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a five-dimensional bulk spacetime containing a three-dimensional Robertson–Walker brane coupled to a bulk scalar field φ. The bulk metric is taken to be of warped form
  ds² = a(Y)² [ -dt² + R(t)² γ_{ij}(k) dx^i dx^j ] + dY²,
where Y is the extra (transverse) coordinate, a(Y) is the warp factor, R(t) is the Robertson–Walker scale factor on the brane, and γ_{ij}(k) is the metric of a maximally symmetric 3-space of spatial curvature k ∈ {-1,0,+1}. The scalar field φ = φ(Y) depends only on the transverse coordinate, with bulk action
  S_bulk = ∫ d⁵x √(-g) [ (1/2κ²) R₅ - (1/2)(∂φ)² - V(φ) ],
together with a brane action localized on the 3-brane and a brane tension/potential.

The resulting Einstein–scalar equations form an autonomous system of ODEs in Y (after substitution of the Robertson–Walker ansatz on the brane). Apply the method of asymptotic splittings: decompose the dominant balances of the system, classify all possible asymptotic behaviors of (a, φ) as Y approaches a finite or infinite value, and determine which dominant balances correspond to formal Puiseux/Fuchsian series solutions that are regular (free of curvature and scalar-field singularities) on the brane.

Question: 
(a) For which choices of bulk potential V(φ), brane potential, and spatial curvature k do globally regular asymptotic solutions (regular bulk warp factor a(Y) and regular scalar profile φ(Y), with finite curvature invariants) exist for the coupled brane–bulk system?
(b) Among such regular asymptotic solutions, do any realize the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant, in the sense that the induced four-dimensional cosmological constant on the brane vanishes (or is dynamically driven to zero) without fine-tuning of the brane tension?
(c) How does the role of the spatial curvature k modify the existence and stability of these regular self-tuning solutions, in comparison with the analogous Minkowski-brane case (k=0 with R(t)=const)?
artifact.status_search_result: Self-tuning of the 4D cosmological constant in 5D brane-world setups with bulk scalar fields remains an active area of research. Recent works (e.g., 2017 holographic self-tuning, 2020 bulk-black-hole self-tuning, 2022 P(X,φ) brane-world self-tuning, and 2024 contributions) propose partial mechanisms but a general classification of regular asymptotic Robertson–Walker brane solutions and a fully successful, generic self-tuning resolution of the cosmological constant problem (especially with brane curvature k ≠ 0) has not been established. The problem is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Self-tuning of the cosmological constant in brane-worlds with P(X,φ)
status_evidence.snippet: Revisits the idea of self-tuning the observed cosmological constant to a vanishing value and promotes it to a selection criterion of brane-world models with a 3-brane embedded in a 5d bulk and a bulk scalar with general P(X,φ) Lagrangian.
status_evidence.claim: Self-tuning of the cosmological constant on a 3-brane in a 5D bulk with a scalar field is still being investigated as a viable mechanism, indicating the problem is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Brane cosmology and the self-tuning of the cosmological constant in the presence of bulk black holes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies self-tuning of the cosmological constant on a brane in 5D bulk with black holes; mechanism works under restricted conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Self-tuning solutions in 5D brane setups exist only under specific conditions, and a general resolution remains absent.

status_evidence.title: Holographic self-tuning of the cosmological constant
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a holographic self-tuning mechanism in brane-bulk setups with a scalar; partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Holographic self-tuning is a partial proposal that has not closed the cosmological constant problem in the brane-scalar setting.
